requirement: Implement TimeoutHTTPAdapter and create_timeout_session enforcing default connect and read timeouts on all requests. It must validate that timeouts are strictly positive, replace timeout=None with default_timeout in send(), preserve caller-specified positive timeouts, and mount the adapter to both http:// and https:// schemes.
skeleton: TimeoutHTTPAdapter subclass of HTTPAdapter and create_timeout_session factory enforcing non-null timeouts.
caption: A requests transport adapter that guarantees every outgoing call carries a validated timeout. TimeoutValue is a PEP 695 type alias for a single float or a connect-and-read pair of floats. TimeoutHTTPAdapter subclasses HTTPAdapter and takes default_timeout, defaulting to the pair 3.05 and 27.0, which it validates at construction, forwarding any other keyword arguments to the parent. The static _validate_timeout accepts a tuple only when it has exactly two elements, raising ValueError otherwise, requires both elements to be numbers, raising TypeError otherwise, and raises ValueError unless both are strictly positive, returning them as floats; a scalar must also be strictly positive or ValueError is raised, and any other type raises TypeError. send(request, *args, **kwargs) keeps the parent's signature compatible: it substitutes the adapter default when the timeout keyword is missing or None, and otherwise validates and keeps the caller's own value, so an explicit 12.5 is forwarded unchanged instead of being overwritten, before delegating to the parent send. create_timeout_session(default_timeout) builds a requests.Session and mounts one such adapter on both the http:// and https:// prefixes. The fixture asserts the rejection of malformed, non-numeric, zero, and negative timeouts, the default substitution, the preservation of caller-supplied timeouts, and that a session created with 5.0 and 15.0 carries that default on both schemes.

plan.intent: Make every outgoing HTTP request carry a validated timeout
constraints: A timeout is a positive float or a pair of positive floats
A tuple of the wrong length or a non-positive value raises ValueError, and a non-numeric value raises TypeError
A missing or None timeout is replaced by the adapter default
A caller's explicit timeout is kept as given
A session factory mounts the adapter on both http and https

rationale.teaches: An HTTPAdapter subclass that enforces a (connect, read) default timeout, validates positivity, respects a caller's explicit positive timeout, and is mounted on both schemes.
rationale.why: requests has no default timeout, so an unmodified adapter hangs forever on a silent peer. The fixture intercepts send and reads the effective timeout, since a real hang cannot be tested.

ops.docstring: Requests timeout enforcing HTTP adapter and session factory.

ops.source:
def create_timeout_session(
    default_timeout: TimeoutValue = (3.05, 27.0),
) -> requests.Session:
    """Return a session with a TimeoutHTTPAdapter mounted for http and https."""
    session = requests.Session()
    adapter = TimeoutHTTPAdapter(default_timeout=default_timeout)
    session.mount("http://", adapter)
    session.mount("https://", adapter)
    return session

candidates.why_wrong: The default timeout is a single 60 second value, so connect and read share one budget instead of the separate 3.05 and 27 seconds.
Zero and negative timeouts are accepted, so a caller can disable the timeout by passing 0.
The check uses <, so a timeout of exactly 0 is accepted.
The caller's timeout is always overridden with the default, so a request that needs a longer read timeout cannot get one.
A plain HTTPAdapter is mounted instead of TimeoutHTTPAdapter, so no default timeout is ever applied.
